title: FMCC: Flexible Measurement-based Quantum Computation over Cluster State
problem: Cluster state depth in measurement-based quantum computing (MBQC) over photonic systems significantly impacts execution time and circuit error rates. Existing MBQC compilation approaches do not efficiently minimize this critical depth parameter.
motivation: MBQC is a promising quantum computing paradigm for photonic systems where cluster state depth directly determines performance, making optimization essential for practical photonic quantum computers.
method: FMCC uses dynamic programming with heuristics to optimize the ordering and dependencies of one-way measurements on photonic cluster states (2-D entangled photon meshes). The compiler framework systematically explores measurement sequences to minimize overall cluster state depth while maintaining quantum circuit correctness.
key_novelty: Dynamic programming with heuristics to efficiently minimize cluster state depth in measurement-based quantum computing on photonic platforms.
contributions: FMCC compilation framework for optimizing cluster state depth in photonic MBQC systems
Dynamic programming algorithm with heuristic pruning for minimizing measurement sequence length
51.7%, 57.4%, and 56.8% average depth reductions over state-of-the-art MBQC compilers for small, medium, and large qubit counts respectively
limitations: Paper abstract does not explicitly discuss limitations or constraints.
primary_theme: quantum circuit compilation for photonic systems
